hero.title: Keep the display awake. Be precise about presence.
hero.lede: TinyNudge is a browser mouse jiggler and mouse mover for people who need the screen to stay on during reads, exports, and presentations — without installing software or asking IT for admin rights.
hero.note: This page can keep the monitor from sleeping. It cannot move your system cursor. Desktop Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Discord still watch real input idle. If you need the green status on those apps, use the Mac menu-bar app or a USB jiggler — and only where your workplace allows it.

two.title: Two tools, two jobs
two.web.p: Uses the Screen Wake Lock API, with a quiet audio fallback, so the display does not dim while this tab is available. Works on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Chromebooks in a current Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox window.
two.mac.p: A menu-bar mouse jiggler that offsets the real pointer a few pixels and returns it. That is the same class of signal a USB mouse jiggler sends, without another dongle. Use it when desktop chat still flips to Away.
how.title: How to keep your computer awake
how.1.p: No extension, installer, or administrator password. A normal browser tab is enough.
how.2.p: TinyNudge requests a screen wake lock. The status lamps show which APIs actually ran.
how.3.p: Keep the window restored, or use picture-in-picture so the lock can survive a tab switch.

use.title: What this is for
use.lead: People usually want one of three outcomes: the screen stays bright, a kiosk does not lock, or a chat status stays available. Those are different technical problems. TinyNudge labels them instead of mixing them into one promise.
use.screen.p: Long PDFs, lecture videos, photo exports, and unattended downloads. The browser tool is built for this. It is the same idea as leaving a video tab open, with a dedicated wake lock.
use.kiosk.p: Lobby displays and workshop machines often sleep on the default energy profile. A wake lock or a hardware jiggler keeps the panel on without changing system settings for every user.
use.chat.p: Desktop clients treat “no keyboard or mouse” as idle. A website cannot reset that timer. Read the status guide before you assume a browser tab will keep the green dot.
what.title: What is a mouse jiggler?
what.p1: A mouse jiggler (also called a mouse mover) is any device or program that stops a computer from treating you as gone. The common symptoms are display sleep, a lock screen, a screensaver, or chat flipping from Available to Away. Hardware jigglers are USB sticks. Software jigglers are Mac or Windows apps. An online mouse jiggler is a webpage — the fastest option when you cannot install software.
what.p2: Browsers are sandboxed. They can ask the operating system to keep the display on. They cannot synthesize HID mouse events. If a site claims it will move your cursor or keep desktop Slack green from a webpage alone, that claim is stronger than the web platform allows. TinyNudge states the split on the first screen.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Does this online mouse jiggler move my real mouse?
faq.a1: No. The moving pointer on the card is a preview. Your system cursor stays put. That is a browser security rule, not a missing feature.
faq.q2: Will Slack or Microsoft Teams stay green?
faq.a2: Desktop apps watch keyboard and mouse idle, not whether a tab holds a wake lock. This page keeps the screen awake. For status idle on a Mac, use TinyNudge for Mac or a hardware jiggler — and follow your employer’s policy.
faq.a3: No. If you can open a website, you can run the online mouse mover.
faq.q4: Does it work on Mac, Windows, and Chromebook?
faq.a4: Yes, in a modern browser. Wake Lock is most reliable in Chrome and Edge. Safari 16.4+ and recent Firefox are supported; the silent-audio fallback covers older gaps.
faq.q5: How do I get TinyNudge for Mac?
faq.a5: Download the disk image from the Mac app page. It is free. For install help, use contact.
faq.a6: Yes. The website and TinyNudge for Mac are free. One download runs on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
faq.q7: Is a mouse jiggler the same as an auto clicker?
faq.a7: No. A jiggler only concerns movement or wake. An auto clicker sends click events. TinyNudge does not click buttons or fill forms.
faq.a8: The jiggler runs locally in your browser. See the privacy policy. No account is required.

page.privacy.title: Privacy — TinyNudge
page.privacy.p1: TinyNudge’s online mouse jiggler runs in your browser using the Screen Wake Lock API, optional silent audio, and optional Picture-in-Picture. Session state never leaves your device. We do not require an account, and we do not record mouse coordinates, keystrokes, or screen contents.
page.privacy.p2: Use the contact form for questions. Do not send passwords.
page.privacy.p3: This static site may be hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare. Those providers see normal web logs (IP address, user agent) as with any website. The contact form is delivered by Formsubmit so we can receive messages without publishing an inbox on the page. Formsubmit and we see the name, email, and message you submit. We do not run advertising or analytics scripts on this version. TinyNudge is not a tool for bypassing employer monitoring or security software.
page.privacy.p4: TinyNudge for Mac is a free download. See TinyNudge for Mac.
